preconditions.description: All input lines after the first contain exactly one string each (no whitespace).
The first line is an integer n where 1 ≤ n ≤ 100.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= len(s) <= 100 for s in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
preconditions.description: Each string has length between 1 and 100, inclusive.

preconditions.expression: all(all(c in 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz' for c in s) for s in [line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
preconditions.description: Each string consists only of lowercase English letters.

postconditions.description: If no valid ordering exists, output is exactly 'NO'. Otherwise, output is 'YES' followed by exactly n strings (one per line).

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'YES' and all(s1 in s2 for s1, s2 in zip(output_strings, output_strings[1:]))
postconditions.description: If output is 'YES', then for every string in the output list (except the last), all strings before it must be substrings of it. Here, output_strings = [line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]] if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else [].

postconditions.expression: stdout.strip() == 'NO' or set(output_strings) == set([line.strip() for line in stdin.splitlines()[1:]])
postconditions.description: If output is 'YES', then the multiset of strings in the output must exactly match the input multiset. Here, output_strings = [line.strip() for line in stdout.splitlines()[1:]] if stdout.strip() == 'YES' else [].
